To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the aging of cardiac muscle cells is characterized by a decrease in the expression of genes that regulate mitochondrial function and cardiac-specific transcription, and by the expression of genes involved in the development of heart failure.
the aging process of cardiac muscle cells is characterized by changes in the expression of a number of genes.
aging cardiac myocytes show reduced levels of genes involved in cellular adaptation and stress protection together with the development and development of contractile dysfunctions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes whose expression changes with cardiac aging.
the identification of genes whose expression is altered with aging in the heart.
the molecular basis of aging-related changes in the cardiac myocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cardiac myocytes undergo a process of senescence that may contribute to the development of age-related cardiac dysfunction.
the aging heart displays a profile of gene expression that reflects the aging process and is associated with the development of heart failure.
aging is associated with a decrease in the expression of genes that are related to cellular protection, adaptation, and contractile function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aging process of the heart can be described by the expression profiles of the genes in the cardiomyocyte.

aging of the heart may be related in part to the reduced activity of genes that are involved in the regulation of the mitochondrial electron chain and in the maintenance of cardiac muscle cell structure and contractile function.
we were able to identify a set of aging-related changes in the expression of genes in cardiac myocytes that are likely to be involved in the pathogenesis of heart diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular basis of the aging heart is a decrease in cellular adaptation and protection, and the development of contractility defects.
the molecular basis of cardiac aging can be studied in a systematic and unbiased manner by gene expression profiling.
we identified a large number of genes that exhibit changes of mRNA levels in the aging heart.
